fiscal

/FIS-kuhl/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is fiscal is of or relating to financial matters.

The company's fiscal year ends every December thirty-first.

Example

At the school board meeting, the debate never touches classrooms or curriculum. It is all about the coming year's budget: how much tax revenue will arrive, which expenses to cut, and whether the district can end the year without a deficit.

Every question on the table concerns budgets, revenue, and spending, which is exactly the territory the word fiscal covers. Fiscal is more precise than 'money-related' because it is the formal term for matters of budgets and public finances.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

monetary: Monetary means relating to money or currency itself -- coins, bills, exchange rates, the money supply. Fiscal concerns how money is planned and used: budgets, taxes, revenue, and spending. A nation's monetary questions are about its currency; its fiscal questions are about its budget.

budgetary: Budgetary means relating to a budget -- the planned income and spending of one organization or program. Fiscal covers that territory and more: taxes, revenue, and the whole formal management of money by governments and institutions. Budgetary points at one plan; fiscal names the whole field.

money-related: Money-related is the loose, everyday label for anything touching money at all -- allowances, prices, tips. Fiscal is the formal term reserved for budgets, taxes, and the finances of governments and organizations. A question about lunch money is money-related; a government budget plan is fiscal.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

nonmonetary: not involving money or payment

ceremonial: done for show or tradition rather than practical money matters

Where it sits · how narrowly it points to budgets — economic → commercial → financial → fiscal

economic vs. fiscal: Economic is broader and weaker than fiscal — economic issues cover jobs, prices, and resources in general, while fiscal issues focus tightly on budgets and money management.

commercial vs. fiscal: Commercial is weaker than fiscal; commercial matters involve buying and selling, but fiscal matters involve the serious business of taxes, budgets, and spending plans.

financial vs. fiscal: Financial is slightly weaker and less specific than fiscal — financial can describe any money matter, while fiscal usually points to official budgets and government or company finances.

Put it together

Put it together: Fisc (the Roman treasury — originally a woven money basket) + -al (relating to): fiscal means relating to the treasury — money, budgets, and finances.
